questions.stem: The male gamete in humans is the:
questions.explanation: Male gamete = spermatozoon (haploid, n=23 chromosomes), produced in testes under FSH/LH + testosterone. Female gamete = ovum (n=23). Fusion → zygote (2n=46). Embryo is the multicellular stage after cleavage. Spermatogenesis is continuous from puberty; oogenesis begins before birth and arrests till ovulation.

questions.stem: Human pregnancy (from the last menstrual period) typically lasts approximately:
questions.explanation: Gestation averages 40 weeks from LMP (~38 weeks post-conception), or about 280 days. Full-term is 37-42 weeks; below 37 is preterm. Pregnancy is divided into three trimesters. Elephants have the longest mammalian gestation (~22 months).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Fertilisation in humans normally takes place in the:
questions.explanation: Sperm–ovum fusion occurs in the ampulla (widest region) of the fallopian tube. The zygote then takes ~6-10 days to reach the uterus and implant. Implantation outside the uterus — most often in the fallopian tube itself — is called an ectopic pregnancy and is a medical emergency.

questions.stem: Which hormone is detected in a standard urine pregnancy test?
questions.explanation: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) is secreted by the placenta soon after implantation and maintains the corpus luteum, which in turn secretes progesterone. hCG is detectable in urine from about day 10-14 post-fertilisation, peaks around week 10, then declines. Estrogen and progesterone also support pregnancy but are not used in the standard strip test.

questions.stem: The biological sex of a human child is determined at the time of:
questions.explanation: The sperm carries either an X or a Y chromosome; the ovum always carries an X. X-sperm + X-ovum → XX (girl); Y-sperm + X-ovum → XY (boy). So the father's sperm determines sex at fertilisation. The SRY gene on the Y chromosome drives male gonadal development from about week 6-7 of embryogenesis.

questions.stem: The world's first baby conceived through IVF was:
questions.explanation: Louise Brown — world's first IVF baby, born 25 July 1978 in Oldham, UK; Drs Robert Edwards and Patrick Steptoe led the team (Edwards received the Nobel in 2010). India's first IVF baby was Kanupriya ('Durga'), born 3 October 1978 in Kolkata to Dr Subhash Mukhopadhyay — just 67 days after Louise Brown. Elizabeth Carr was the US first, 1981. Victoria Anna was Australia's first, 1980.

questions.stem: On average, the human menstrual cycle lasts about:
questions.explanation: The average cycle is 28 days, with a normal range of 21-35 days between healthy adult women. Ovulation occurs around day 14. Menstruation typically lasts 3-7 days. The cycle is governed by the hypothalamic–pituitary–ovarian axis via GnRH, FSH, LH, estrogen and progesterone.
